text:
jess: quick sync — thinking out loud about the continuous-batcher split. two viable paths: keep the admission + coalesce in one runtime (current), or split into a lightweight admission plane + separate coalescer/packer service. tradeoffs?

omar: splitting seems cleaner for ownership and testing, but worried about cross-plane latency and extra RPCs.

maria: agree on ownership. also we currently have an observability blindspot around 'coalesce effectiveness' once things are shunted through the runtime. splitting could make it easier to surface metrics like `coalesce_rate` and `eviction_amplification`.

kevin: fwiw, single-process has fewer moving parts and lower p99 for tiny requests. experiments show ~2ms less tail when admission and coalesce share memory. adding RPC hop could add 0.5-1.5ms median and higher tail if network jitter.

jess: good point. main arguments I see:
- split: clearer interfaces, independent scaling, easier incremental rollout, per-plane telemetry and feature flags
- monolith: lowest hop count, simpler debug story, shared mem for KV warmup and slot accounting

maria: another dimension — failure modes. with split, we can make coalescer opportunistic: drop/merge under pressure and degrade gracefully. But need a robust fallback path so admission can route to a safe slowpath model directly if coalescer is unreachable.

omar: what about the contract between admission <> coalescer? we should avoid per-request heavyweight metadata. propose a tiny opaque token and `deadline_hint_ms` and `tenant_headroom` for packing. minimal wire fields reduce serialization cost.

kevin: +1. sample proto sketch:```
message PackHint {
  uint64 token = 1;
  uint32 deadline_hint_ms = 2;
  uint32 token_count = 3; // estimated tokens for batch shaping
  bool prefer_low_latency = 4;
}
```
keep it minimal.

jess: telemetry gap: currently we only emit batch_size, batch_wait_ms, and eviction_count at runtime. after split we should add: `coalesce_success_rate`, `pack_latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}`, `headroom_pressure` (per-tenant), and `kv_warmup_miss`. these will drive optimizer recommendations.

maria: agree. also add a derived metric: `effective_tokens_per_batch` to detect quantization of small requests that kill efficiency.

omar: rollout strategy idea: feature flag `split_batcher_v1` default off. route 5% of traffic from a canary nodepool through the split path with circuit breaker to fallback. measure token_cost_delta, p99_tail_delta, and coalesce_loss_rate.

kevin: perf budget: if p99 increases > 3ms or token_cost savings < 5% then auto-disable. otherwise ramp to 25% then 100%.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for split_batcher_v1 on pool batcher-canary-3 at 1799123465 :rocket:

jess: nice — TODOs: 1) Omar to prototype minimal admission <> coalescer RPC and stub metrics (owner) 2) Maria to draft telemetry spec + dashboards 3) Kevin to run microbench harness and perf baseline 4) I'll write short RFC with rollout plan.

omar: I'll take the prototype, will push initial branch with a bench harness by EOD Friday.

maria: drafting telemetry doc now, will drop a PR with dashboard mockups.

kevin: I'll wire up the microbench and simulate 1k tenants with skewed token distributions. will report p50/p95/p99 and token-economics.

jess: last concern — KV cache locality: if coalescer is separate, we either replicate small KVs to the coalescer or keep it in admission and expose a warmup API. prefer warmup API to avoid replication complexity. add `kv_warmup_hint` to PackHint.

omar: noted. warmup API can be async: `warmup(token)` and return `warmup_status`. will stub now.

maria: one more ops note: alerts. add alert `coalesce_failure_rate > 1% for 5m` and `pack_queue_length > threshold` to avoid silent efficiency regressions.

jess: perfect. If no objections I'll convert this into an RFC draft and link the prototype once Omar opens the branch. :thumbsup:

kevin: no objections from me. excited to see numbers. :eyes:

omar: ack. starting work.

sre-bot: incident-bot: reminder — page rotations for eng-runtime on-call this week: kevin -> maria -> omar.

jess: thanks team — filing the RFC now and tagging you all.
